chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan and Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a woman whose husband has died, whether she observes her waiting period (iddah) in her own house or wherever she wishes. He said, 'Rather, wherever she wishes. Indeed, when 'Umar died, 'Ali (peace be upon him) came to Umm Kulthum and took her to his house.'

key_terms.أُمَّ كُلْثُومٍ: Umm Kulthum (daughter of Ali and Fatimah)
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُ: widow (literally: the woman whose husband has died)

ai.seo_question: Where should a widow reside during her Islamic waiting period (iddah)?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a widow's residence during her *iddah* is flexible, not strictly confined to the marital home, based on the precedent of Imam Ali (AS) relocating Umm Kulthum bint Ali to his own house after Umar's death. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the widow's autonomy and practical convenience, distinguishing it from stricter interpretations found in other schools. The incident serves as a crucial *sunna* for understanding the spatial flexibility granted to widows during their waiting period.
